messages.content: What's the population in New York right now?

function.name: time_converter
function.description: Converts the local time of user's region to the target region's local time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_timezone.description: The timezone of the user in string format. Example: 'Pacific Time (US & Canada)'

target_timezone.description: The target timezone in string format where user wants to know the local time. Example: 'Eastern Time (US & Canada)'

time.description: The local time of user's timezone in string format (24 hr format). Optional parameter. Example: '15:30:00'

message.content: The most recent estimates put the population of New York City at roughly **8.5 million people**. This figure comes from the U.S. Census Bureau’s annual population estimates and reflects the city’s growth over the past few years. Population numbers change gradually, so the exact count at any given moment will be close to this estimate.
message.reasoning: User asks: "What's the population in New York right now?" They want current population. We can approximate or use known data. The population of New York City is about 8.5 million. But "right now" might refer to current estimate. We can provide approximate. Also mention that population changes slowly. Provide source: US Census. Provide approximate.
